cohort: 72 pregnant women diagnosed with hyperprolactinemia, 66 of whom were using dopamine agonists (cabergoline or bromocriptine), identified from a larger cohort of 464 women at an endocrine gynecology outpatient clinic of a tertiary hospital.
finding: Regardless of the type of previous drug treatment with dopamine agonists, hyperprolactinemia did not alter obstetric outcomes.
mod_finding: There was no difference in the type of delivery according to the type of treatment used (cabergoline or bromocriptine) or the presence of hyperprolactinemia.
